sample_unit: admissions (paired physician and LLM hospital courses)

links.outcome: Attending-rated confabulation in LLM vs physician hospital courses after resident editing
links.effect: LLM HCs contained more confabulations than physician HCs (mean [SD] difference -0.98 [3.53]; P = .002) on 10-point bidirectional scale.
links.quote: Attending physicians deemed LLM HCs to be more complete (mean [SD] difference LLM vs physicians on 10-point bidirectional scale, 3.00 [5.28]; P < .001), similarly concise (mean [SD], -1.02 [6.08]; P = .20), and cohesive (mean [SD], 0.70 [6.14]; P = .60), but with more confabulations (mean [SD], -0.98 [3.53]; P = .002).

unlisted_practices: Physician editing of LLM-drafted hospital course summaries measured by percentage edited and semantic change
Blinded A/B comparison of LLM vs physician hospital course on completeness, conciseness, cohesion, and confabulation (4Cs)

screen.reason: Empirical study testing resident physician editing and hospitalist evaluation of LLM-generated vs physician-generated hospital course discharge summaries in a simulated/retrospective reader study. It does not compare outcomes with vs without an organizational deployment safeguard.
